newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee edges up to close at 35.70 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee edges up to close at 35.70 per dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.7000/7050 against the dollar on Monday, up from the day's opening quote of 35.73/74, dealers said.
Dealers said a Calcutta-based bank was active in the morning session, followed by some Bombay banks. The rupee edged up to 35.71/72 level soon after, dealers said.
Most of the day's business was at 35.70 level though there were quotes at 35.6950/7050, a dealer at a state-run bank said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought some stray amounts at 35.7050 level in the afternoon. "They bought some from three or four local banks," said the chief dealer of a Bombay bank.
"But it didn't affect the exchange rate," he said.
Premia in the forward dollar market were lower on Monday largely because of the unusually low call rates, dealers said.
Call rates closed at 0.25-0.75 percent, down from the opening rate of 1.25-2.00 percent, dealers said.

Newspaper reports quoting the RBI governor on Monday as saying the central bank was contemplating a fresh cut in cash reserve ratio for banks in January also affected sentiment in the call market, dealers said.
The six-month annualised premium fell to 8.06 percent towards the close on Monday, down from the weekend close of 8.45 percent, dealers said.
Chief dealers at two leading banks -- one state-run and the other foreign -- said they did not expect any major fluctuation in the rupee-dollar exchange rate in December.
But some companies expect the rupee to fall from current levels before the New Year.
"It should touch 35.80/90 levels before New Year," R.K. Das, chief of forex and treasury at Adani Exports told Reuters.
He said the current level cannot be sustained. "One bout of (dollar) demand is enough to push (the rupee) to that level."
